Stryker plans a roughly $400 million CMR Surgical investment

The alliance includes U.S. sales rights and a future acquisition option, subject to conditions.

Stryker / GlobeNewswire ↗12 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Investment with a future option

Stryker and CMR Surgical announced a planned preferred-equity investment of approximately $400 million, or £300 million. Stryker also receives an exclusive future option to acquire the remaining equity under agreed terms; a full acquisition has not closed.

Sharing commercial responsibilities

Stryker will be the exclusive U.S. sales agent for the Versius portfolio. CMR retains product development and commercialization outside the United States, combining its soft-tissue robotics expertise with Stryker’s commercial network.

Conditions and clinical limits

The companies highlight Versius’s modular operating-room design, but this announcement is not comparative clinical evidence. Regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions remain, and commercial expansion should not be confused with demonstrated treatment superiority or authorization in every country.
